findings.title: Dynamic imports are invoked eagerly, defeating the lazy-loading goal
findings.body: The appStore object calls `import("./applecalendar")` etc. at module-evaluation time, so every app package is loaded as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported. The only difference from the previous static imports is that consumers now have to `await` the values; nothing is actually deferred (bundle size and startup cost are unchanged, and in webpack all chunks are requested immediately). To get real async loading the values must be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites doing `await appStore[key]()`.

findings.title: Eagerly created import promises can produce unhandled rejections
findings.body: Because each `import(...)` promise is created at module load, any app module that throws during initialization (e.g. missing env/app keys) produces a rejected promise that nobody is awaiting at that moment. In Node this surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection and can crash the process (or at minimum log a fatal warning), even for apps the request never touches. With lazy thunks the rejection would only occur where it is awaited and handled.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in the `calendar` field, breaking external consumers
findings.body: `getCalendar` became async, but `getCalendarCredentials` still stores its result synchronously, so `item.calendar` is now a `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it, but any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that uses `.calendar` directly (e.g. to call `listCalendars()`/`getAvailability()`) will now be operating on a Promise and fail at runtime. Either make `getCalendarCredentials` async and resolve the calendars, or audit/update all consumers.

findings.title: async forEach pushes deletions into apiDeletes after they are awaited
findings.body: In the recurring-cancellation branch the callback is `async` and now awaits `getCalendar(credential)` before pushing into `apiDeletes`. The surrounding `forEach` does not wait, so execution continues to `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) while `apiDeletes` is still empty; the calendar deletions are fired after the response is computed and their errors become unhandled rejections. Replace with a `for ... of` loop and await, or collect the promises synchronously.

findings.title: Unused awaited calendar in recurring branch
findings.body: `const calendar = await getCalendar(calendarCredential)` is computed before the branch, but in the recurring path a new `calendar` is fetched inside the loop, so the outer one is unused. This performs an unnecessary credential/calendar instantiation (and now an extra module load) on every recurring cancellation.

findings.title: async callback inside forEach escapes the try/catch and is never awaited
findings.body: Changing the `forEach` callback to `async` means the returned promises are discarded: the enclosing `try/catch` can no longer catch failures of `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` (they become unhandled rejections), and the function returns/sends the reschedule email before the calendar/video events are actually deleted. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` instead.

findings.title: async callback inside forEach escapes the try/catch and is never awaited
findings.body: Same issue as the vital reschedule: making the `forEach` callback `async` means its promise is dropped, so errors from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` bypass the surrounding `try/catch` and become unhandled rejections, and the function continues (sending emails, returning true) before the external events are deleted. Use `Promise.all` over `map` and await it.

findings.title: requestReschedule fires calendar/video deletions without awaiting them
findings.body: The `forEach` callback is now `async` and awaits `getCalendar`, but the loop does not await the resulting promises. The mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns while deletions are still pending; in a serverless environment the function may terminate before they run, leaving stale calendar/video events, and any error becomes an unhandled rejection. Collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.all`.

findings.title: Noisy info log of CalendarService on every getCalendar call
findings.body: `log.info("calendarApp", calendarApp.lib.CalendarService)` logs the service class on every calendar resolution, which now happens on every booking/cancel/availability path. This is debug-level noise in production logs and should be removed or downgraded.
